Raise a registered refusal

Source: R/refusal_taxonomy.R
fb_refuse.Rd

fb_refuse() stops with a refusal condition for a reason registered by flexyBayes or by a package through fb_register_refusals(). The condition has the classes flexybayes_refusal_<reason_code>, any classes given in class, and flexybayes_refusal, so users catch a plug-in's refusals exactly as they catch the core's.

Usage

fb_refuse(reason_code, message = NULL, ..., class = character(0), call = NULL)

Arguments

reason_code

A registered reason code (see fb_refusals()).

message

The message shown to the user. Defaults to the reason's registered description. A message that names the user's own variables or values is usually more helpful.

...

Further named fields to carry on the condition object, for handlers that need the offending value. The names message, reason_code, package and call are set by fb_refuse() and cannot be used.

class

Additional condition classes, placed between the per-code class and flexybayes_refusal.

call

The call to record on the condition. Defaults to NULL, as for the core's refusals.

Value

Does not return. It signals an error. The condition carries message, reason_code, package (the package that registered the code), call and the fields given in ....

See also

fb_register_refusals(), fb_refusals().

Examples

res <- tryCatch(
  fb_refuse("unsupported_family"),
  flexybayes_refusal = function(e) e
)
res$reason_code
#> [1] "unsupported_family"
res$package
#> [1] "flexyBayes"
